notes.text: GCO's handler reads a `playerID`; the Companion lists none. Not seen in vanilla handlers (they take no arguments).
There is an eighth argument, `activationValue`, after `activationType`; the Companion lists seven. Also, the first two arguments are the plot x, y.
notes.evidence: vanilla Lua (TutorialUIRoot.lua OnImprovementActivated) and GCO PlotScript.lua:2457

notes.text: GCO's handler declares six arguments `(playerID, cityID, productionID, objectID, bCanceled, typeModifier)`; the Companion lists five. A sixth value probably exists but its meaning is unconfirmed. Vanilla handlers only use the first two.
GCO declares a third argument (a cancelled flag, as CivicCompleted has); the Companion lists two.
GCO's handlers read `x, y`; the Companion lists no parameters (vanilla handler ignores them). Same for RouteRemovedFromMap.
Carries only `x, y`, not the feature type. To know which feature was removed, cache the feature per plot yourself (see the event-order page). Same for FeatureRemovedFromMap.
Also fires when a unit moves onto the tile of a unit it has just defeated, so it is not only for real teleports.
Fires once per step of a move; use UnitMoveComplete for once per command. Changing game state from this handler may desync multiplayer (author's warning).

Fires after the engine has already healed or damaged the unit, with `(playerID, unitID, newDamage, prevDamage)`. GCO calls `unit:SetDamage(prevDamage)` in the handler to cancel unwanted healing (it observed that pillaging units are healed by the engine).
For the REMOVE_FEATURE operation the feature is already gone and the builder may already be off the map when this fires.
Fires after CityAddedToMap; city plots are not initialised yet at CityAddedToMap.
When this fires, policy queries (such as `HasPolicyActive` passed from the UI) may still return the old value. GCO delays its recalculation with a coroutine. Same for GovernmentPolicyChanged.
The author calls it the first general event after all CityProductionCompleted events of that player.
